choices.content: Through \(A\), draw a line parallel to \(l\), and mark off a segment of equal length on the other side of \(l\).
Draw an arc centered at \(A\) with any radius, intersecting \(l\) at one point. That point is the required point.
Join \(A\) to any point \(P\) on \(l\) and extend to \(A'\) so that \(PA'=PA\).
Through \(A\), draw a perpendicular to \(l\), with foot \(O\). On the perpendicular on the other side, mark \(A'\) so that \(OA'=OA\). Then \(A'\) is the required point.

question.prompt: How do you construct the reflection of point \(A\) across line \(l\)?

solutions.explanation: The segment joining a point and its reflection is perpendicularly bisected by the axis of reflection, so first construct a perpendicular, then locate a point at the same distance.
solutions.title: Perpendicular bisector construction
